rows.verdict: Z1 has lower package-internal loss in HV-S0; Z2 has lower package-internal loss in HV-S1 (each gap exceeds twice the measured discretisation uncertainty): the package-internal loss ordering reverses with the scenario. HV-S2 is not rankable because the Z1 operating point is physically inadmissible for the solid-solder model.

Z1 has lower peak temperature in HV-S0; Z2 has lower peak temperature in HV-S1 (each gap exceeds twice the measured discretisation uncertainty): the peak temperature ordering reverses with the scenario. HV-S2 is not rankable because the Z1 operating point is physically inadmissible for the solid-solder model.

Z1 has lower die warpage in every scenario for which a valid two-architecture comparison can be made; HV-S2 is not rankable because the Z1 operating point is physically inadmissible for the solid-solder model.

Z1 has lower joint displacement driver in every scenario for which a valid two-architecture comparison can be made; HV-S2 is not rankable because the Z1 operating point is physically inadmissible for the solid-solder model.

Z1 has lower local inelastic response in HV-S0; Z2 has lower local inelastic response in HV-S1 (each gap exceeds twice the measured discretisation uncertainty): the local inelastic response ordering reverses with the scenario. HV-S2 is not rankable because the Z1 operating point is physically inadmissible for the solid-solder model.

per_scenario.HV_S0: Z1 lower for any feed resistance
per_scenario.HV_S1: conditional: Z2 lower only below R* = 3.16 mOhm

rows.verdict: The platform-inclusive loss has no unconditional winner: in HV-S0 Z1 has the lower platform-inclusive loss for any feed resistance; in HV-S1 Z2 has the lower platform-inclusive loss only while the complete direct-feed loop stays below R* = 3.16 mOhm, and Z1 above it; HV-S2 is not rankable (the Z1 operating point is inadmissible). No value of that loop resistance is known, so no platform-level ranking is claimed.
